what: Introduction: The Lifeblood of Clinical Research
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: clinical investigators, calculating sample size often critical step preparing grant proposals IRB submissions. Underpowered trials risk false-negative findings (P>0.05P > 0.05), wasting research grants patient effort. Conversely, overpowered trials waste resources expose unnecessary subjects experimental risks. sampleSizeCalc package provides complete support 42 specific clinical scenarios, delivering publication-grade LaTeX formulas, primary citations chapter/page numbers, clear parameter roles.

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: α\alpha (Type Error / False Positive): probability declaring treatment effective truly (conventionally 0.05). Power=1−β\text{Power} = 1 - \beta (True Positive Detection): probability catching true effect (routinely 0.80 0.90). Continuous vs. Binary Endpoints: Continuous measures numerical values (mean reduction SBP, mmHg); binary measures event status (cured vs. cured). Two-Sided vs. One-Sided: Two-sided tests differences either direction; one-sided tests used non-inferiority directional superiority. Dropout Rate (dd): Inflation formula Nscreen=⌈N/(1−d)⌉N_{\text{screen}} = \lceil N / (1 - d) \rceil.

id: 引言为什么样本量计算是临床研究的第一生命线
what: 引言：为什么样本量计算是临床研究的第一生命线？
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 很多临床医生在申报国家自然科学基金、撰写临床试验方案（Protocol）或提交伦理审查时，最容易被评审专家质疑的就是样本量计算依据。 不经严谨测算就随意定一个样本量（比如“凭经验随访 50 例”），会面临两大致命风险： 1. 样本量过小（Underpowered，检验效能不足）：哪怕药物真有疗效，因为人数太少，微弱的信号会被人体的抽样波动彻底掩盖，最终 P>0.05P > 0.05，得出“无统计学显著差异”的假阴性结论，浪费科研经费与受试者心血。 2. 样本量过大（Overpowered，不符合医学伦理）：纳入过多患者不仅拖延试验周期，更在伦理上让多余的受试者暴露在未知疗效或有潜在副作用的试验药物中。 sampleSizeCalc（临床研究样本量计算器）覆盖了现代临床科研从经典双臂 RCT、流行病学调查，到前沿的 Simon 两阶段肿瘤试验、生物等效性（）、多阅片者诊断试验（MRMC）以及 BMJ 最新的 Riley 2020 预测模型样本量规则等 42 个具体场景。 每一次计算，都会输出学术级 LaTeX 公式、精确到章节和页码的文献出处、以及参数角色说明，可直接写入申报书与伦理文件！

what: 统计零基础必读：核心概念通俗白话字典
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 通俗比喻：“法官冤枉好人的概率”。新药明明没有用，但巧合之下我们误认为新药有用的概率。 常规取值：国际学术界惯例设为 0.05（即 5%）。单侧检验（如非劣效试验）常设为 0.025 或 0.05。 通俗比喻：“警察抓出真凶的把握”。新药确实有用时，我们的试验能以多大的概率把它检测出来。 常规取值：通常设为 0.80（80%） 或 0.90（90%）。把握度要求越高，需要招募的患者越多。 连续型指标：测量出来是具体数值，如收缩压降幅（mmHg）、空腹血糖（mmol/L）。核心参数是“均数差（Δ\Delta）”与“标准差（σ\sigma, SD）”。 二分类指标：只有“有效/无效”、“治愈/未治愈”，如有效率 80%、死亡率 15%。 双侧检验：事先不确定新药到底会比对照组好还是差，两头都看（经典临床试验通用）。 单侧检验：只关心新药是否优于对照药，或者新药是否“不差于”对照药（非劣效/优效性试验通用）。 随访中患者失访或退出。设计划脱落率为 dd（如 10%），目标样本量需放大：Nscreen=⌈N/(1−d)⌉N_{\text{screen}} = \lceil N / (1 - d) \rceil。

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Comparing means two independent groups (e.g., treatment vs. control) Example: clinical trial comparing mean blood pressure reduction two treatments Interpretation: - Need 37 subjects per group - Total sample size: 74 subjects - effect size (Cohen’s d): 0.67 Formula: $$n = 2\\left(\\frac{(Z_{\\alpha/2} + Z_{\\beta}) \\cdot \\sigma}{\\mu_1 - \\mu_2}\\right)^2$$ Reference: Chow et al. (2017). Sample Size Calculations Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "twoMeans",   mean1 = 10, # Control group mean (mmHg reduction)   mean2 = 12, # Treatment group mean (mmHg reduction)   sd = 3, # Common standard deviation   alpha = 0.05, # Significance level   power = 0.8 # Target power (80%) )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Comparing means paired matched observations (e.g., pre-post measurements, matched pairs) Example: Measuring cognitive function intervention subjects Interpretation: - Need 29 pairs (.e., 58 measurements 29 subjects) - Standardized effect size: 0.62 Reference: Rosner (2015). Fundamentals Biostatistics (8th ed.). Cengage Learning.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "pairedMeans",   meanDiff = 2.5, # Mean difference (post-pre)   sdDiff = 4.0, # SD of differences   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.9 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Comparing proportions two independent groups Example: Comparing response rates two treatments Interpretation: - Need 163 patients per group - Absolute risk reduction: 0.15 - Relative risk increase: 50% Reference: Fleiss et al. (2003). Statistical Methods Rates Proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "twoProportions",   p1 = 0.30, # Control response rate   p2 = 0.45, # Treatment response rate   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Time--event analysis log-rank test Example: Oncology trial comparing overall survival two treatments Important Notes: - calculates number events needed, total sample size - Total sample size = events / event rate - example, event rate 50%, total sample size needed: 494 subjects Formula: $$E = \\frac{(Z_{\\alpha/2} + Z_{\\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\\ln(HR)]^2}$$ Reference: Schoenfeld (1983). Sample-size formula proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "survival",   hr = 0.70, # Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control)   pE = 0.50, # Proportion in experimental group (1:1 randomization)   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Demonstrating new treatment worse standard margin Example: Non-inferiority trial new antidepressant Key Points: - Uses one-sided α (typically 0.025) - Margin Δ defines clinically acceptable difference - New treatment must within Δ standard Reference: Chow et al. (2017). Sample Size Calculations Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "nonInferiorityMeans",   mean1 = 8.0, # New treatment mean   mean2 = 8.5, # Standard treatment mean   sd = 2.0, # Common SD   margin = 1.0, # Non-inferiority margin (Δ)   alpha = 0.025, # One-sided test   power = 0.9 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Demonstrating new treatment better standard Example: Superiority trial new pain medication Key Points: - Uses one-sided α - Effect must exceed margin meaningful - Smaller margin requires larger sample size
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "superiorityMeans",   mean1 = 12.0, # New treatment mean (better)   mean2 = 10.0, # Standard treatment mean   sd = 2.5, # Common SD   margin = 0.5, # Minimal clinically important difference   alpha = 0.025, # One-sided test   power = 0.85 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Demonstrating two treatments equivalent Example: Bioequivalence study Key Points: - Uses TOST (Two One-Sided Tests) procedure - Requires Zβ/2 (larger sample size) - Margin must larger observed difference
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "equivalenceMeans",   mean1 = 100, # Test mean   mean2 = 102, # Reference mean   sd = 5, # Common SD   margin = 5, # Equivalence margin (±5 units)   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Estimating sensitivity specificity given precision Example: Validating new diagnostic test disease X Interpretation: - Target state cases needed: 196 - Total subjects screen: 980 - 20% prevalence, need screen 980 get 196 cases Formula: $$n_{cases} = \\frac{Z_{1-\\alpha/2}^2 \\cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$ Reference: Hajian-Tilaki (2014). Sample size determination diagnostic test studies. Journal Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "diagnosticAccuracySingle",   prob = 0.85, # Expected sensitivity   d = 0.05, # Desired precision (±5%)   prevalence = 0.20, # Disease prevalence   alpha = 0.05 )  print(result)

title: Comprehensive Guide to sampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Estimating AUC confidence interval given width Example: Validating new biomarker’s discriminative ability Key Points: - Calculates cases disease - AUC variance depends AUC value prevalence - Hanley-McNeil method standard approach Reference: Hanley & McNeil (1982). meaning use AUC. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "auc_single",   auc = 0.80, # Expected AUC   d = 0.05, # Half-width of CI (±0.10 total)   prevalence = 0.30,   alpha = 0.05 )  print(result)

Results match PowerTOST::sampleN.TOST bit--bit (e.g., CV=0.25, theta0=1.0 -> N=24, 12/sequence; theta0=0.95 -> N=28, 14/sequence). diagAccuracy (test): Added method = c("asymptotic", "exact").
